decisions.statement: A read across a boundary is refused where no approved parse follows that read in the same block.
The block is the nearest block or source file or clause with the read.
`JSON.parse` is a read across a boundary rather than a parse.
A call to an identifier spelled `parseSomething` is an approved parse.
A write to `process.env` is no read.
A file named `.d.ts` is passed over.
A file named `.generated.ts` or `.generated.tsx` is passed over.
A path with a `__fixtures__` or a `generated` segment is passed over.
This rule is a check of its own rather than a sixteenth rule under `no-refused-syntax`.
A syntax rule has no phase of its own.
A rule landing under `no-refused-syntax` judges every file at change at once.
Folding this check into `no-refused-syntax` takes every site repaired and this page taken away.
Every site the rule names is repaired.
A parse outside the block the read sits in is not seen.
A read followed through a second variable is not seen.
A call to `firstCapture` is an approved parse.
A body read from a `fetch` answer is a read across a boundary.
A file read through `Bun.file` is a read across a boundary.
A file read through `fs` is a read across a boundary.
The standard output of a spawned process is a read across a boundary.
An answer from a named remote procedure is a read across a boundary.
A capture a regular expression took is a read across a boundary.
A call to `requireMatch` or `requireMatchPositional` is an approved parse.
A call to `requireEnv` or `requireGet` or `requireFirst` is an approved parse.
A file named `.test-fixtures.ts` is passed over.

definition: the check refusing a read across a boundary that no parse follows
